title: Ozzie Newsome on the passing of OJ Brigance: “I am devastated and at a loss for words. O.J. was one of the most genuine, sincere people I have ever known. From the moment he arrived in Baltimore, you could feel his energy. His amazing smile, welcoming nature and infectious personality made everyone around him feel like family. “He was a hero to this city long before his courageous battle with ALS and became an even greater inspiration in the way he faced it with the same fight, faith and grace he brought to the football field. “O.J.’s service to our community, to the Ravens and the fight for a cure for ALS will never be forgotten. He was and always will be a beloved mentor and man. With heartfelt sorrow, we extend our deepest sympathies to Chanda and the Brigance family.”

title: Ravens owner Steve Bisciotti on the passing of OJ Brigance: “We are devastated by the awful news that we have lost O.J. Brigance. O.J. was a beloved legend, mentor and man to everyone who was fortunate enough to know him. He was a vibrant person who became one of the first Ravens heroes with his passionate play, including the first tackle in the 2000 Super Bowl. “Known for his big smile and welcoming nature, it was easy to feel a special connection with O.J. from the moment you met him. His infectious smile and the inspirational way he lived and played endeared him to everyone he touched, both inside our building and across this city. “This is a tremendously sad day for Baltimore. O.J. will be remembered for his service to our community, to the Ravens and to the fight to find a cure for ALS. With heavy hearts, the Ravens organization extends our deepest condolences to Chanda and the entire Brigance family. We are saddened by this loss, and O.J.’s spirit will remain part of this community forever.”

title: Mental health action tip for the day… A GRATITUDE LIST. This changed my everyday being and gave me a new way to start each day. I learned this from an actual Thai monk in Ko Samui, Thailand. He asked me to write down 100 things I’m grateful for. At the time I was in a VERY VERY DARK PLACE. Absolutely self loathing, mired in depression and couldn’t see the light at the other side of the tunnel. So this monk asked me to write down 100 things from my whole life. People, I know my life is GREAT, but too often between my ears just sucks and I didn’t sign up for this shit! I was literally stuck at 1 and he asked me, “You like your watch?” Ummm “yeah, I can use things like that?” “Yes,” he said, “It can be anything. What about GOD? You say you’re a big GOD guy? That’s 2. How about your son? You love your son? That’s 3.” He asked me to think of things my whole life and we’ve all had some good moments. I started slow but eventually I got to 100. In the weeks that followed… I read that list every single day. Now, it’s how I start every morning.I do a list of 10 things I’m grateful for from the previous day or coming up today. And you can have some of the same things each day. It’s not restricted… It’s YOUR list. So I now wake up in gratitude instead of anxiety or dread. WAYYY better way to start my day. Let’s keep fighting this fight together!!! #TeamUnbreakable #mentalhealth #mentalwealth

title: Rookie CB Colton Hood got an earful from Harbaugh after objecting to a flag when he interfered with Odell on a red zone fade from Jaxson Dart. Harbaugh pulled Hood off the field and spoke to him immediately. Harbaugh said he made the point not to argue when he pushed the receiver while the ball was in the air. Harbaugh said it's a challenge for every young corner to learn what's allowed as far as contact. "Here's a young corner that's going to be playing a lot of football, so you've got to accelerate the pace with that process." Harbaugh had another conversation with Hood after the period that ended with a bro hug. Deonte Banks and Greg Newsome got the most first-team corner reps today with Hood mixing in. Hood was getting tended to by a trainer at the end of practice. Not sure if that's anything serious. Rookie DT Bobby Jamison-Travis also got checked by doctors/trainers during practice.

title: Alert: YouTube just announced that it’s changing how views are counted on its platform, with a view now counting as soon as a video starts playing or someone enters a live broadcast. The update goes into effect Aug. 24. It was generally understood that a view was counted after a user watched at least 30 seconds of a video, per Tech Crunch. "....We’ve heard that creators want to eliminate this metric confusion and accurately understand their true exposure, which is why we’re making this update," YouTube stated in a community post. The modification should lead to increased YouTube view counts, especially for videos that only briefly capture viewers’ attention.

title: Giants practice in shells (close to full speed but no hitting) just ended: Malik Nabers did one release rep in 1-on-1 routes (no QB or ball), and his right leg didn’t seem to support his plant/cut well. He regained his balance after the stumble but immediately stepped out of the drill Nabers later took his first ‘live’ rep of camp in 11 on 11. Jogged his route with a limp. Took a second rep later and ran it relatively normally Took two more on the goal line, didn’t see a target. Then caught three passes from Jaxson Dart in 7 on 7. Release looked better there but still limping After his third catch, where he jumped a bit and landed uncomfortably, Nabers walked off slapping himself in the helmet. And he didn’t do anything more in team Nabers then left that field and did some individual releases with trainers on another field Practice ended with Abdul Carter pick 6 of Dart after a Kayvon tip, then Ar’Darius Washington INTd Jameis Winston Center John Michael Schmitz is back from his concussion. Suited up and practiced, although his snaps were limited Colton Hood and Bobby Jamison-Travis both received some attention from trainers during the practice OBJ drew a DPI in the end zone on Hood (on a target from Dart). Later, OBJ caught a pass from Jameis and spun the ball down on the ground for the first down. He wore sweats on a hot day and seemed gassed late, also did push ups after turning the wrong way on a deep target DNPs: WR Jalin Hyatt, RB Turbo Miller, DL Josh Tupou A new LB Chandler Martin was on the practice field in a 55 jersey with no number #talkinball @NYDailyNews
summary:
Giants practice in shells (close to full speed but no hitting) just ended:

Nabers later took his first ‘live’ rep of camp in 11 on 11. Jogged his route with a limp. Took a second rep later and ran it relatively normally

Took two more on the goal line, didn’t see a target. Then caught three passes from Jaxson Dart in 7 on 7. Release looked better there but still limping 

After his third catch, where he jumped a bit and landed uncomfortably, Nabers walked off slapping himself in the helmet. And he didn’t do anything more in team

Nabers then left that field and did some individual releases with trainers on another field

Practice ended with Abdul Carter pick 6 of Dart after a Kayvon tip, then Ar’Darius Washington INTd Jameis Winston 

Center John Michael Schmitz is back from his concussion. Suited up and practiced, although his snaps were limited

Colton Hood and Bobby Jamison-Travis both received some attention from trainers during the practice

OBJ drew a DPI in the end zone on Hood (on a target from Dart). Later, OBJ caught a pass from Jameis and spun the ball down on the ground for the first down. He wore sweats on a hot day and seemed gassed late, also did push ups after turning the wrong way on a deep target

DNPs: WR Jalin Hyatt, RB Turbo Miller, DL Josh Tupou 

A new LB Chandler Martin was on the practice field in a 55 jersey with no number #talkinball @NYDailyNews

title: Today was the first time Malik Nabers participated in full-speed team periods during training camp. Definitely a positive step even if it was hard to read his body language at times. Nabers took four reps in 11-on-11 and three reps in 7-on-7 while wearing a red non-contact jersey (practice was in shells, so there was no contact). Nabers wasn’t targeted in 11-on-11 but had catches on all three reps in 7-on-7. His final catch was a leaping grab on a high pass. He slammed the ball as he got up — unclear why. After the 7-on-7 period he went to the side and ran routes with a trainer. That may have been pre-planned because that’s been part of his normal routine. He’s clearly not going 100% yet, but getting back in team drills is a major step.

title: Jalen Hurts Training Camp Stats, Day 12: Monday’s practice was a surprisingly busy one for Jalen Hurts as he was on the field for 30 reps compared to just 8 totals reps for the backups The only really noteworthy throw of the day from Hurts was a deep pass over the middle that was intercepted. The pass was intended for Quez Watkins but Michael Carter beat him to the spot, was more physical at the catch point and came away with the ball Outside of that it was mostly short throws for Hurts. One of his passes to Goedert was dropped. Another pass along the sideline was slightly overthrown. He also had another throw across his body today, which he has been doing a surprising amount this summer. He is, however, completing a very high percentage of those throws There was also a play where a ball pitched back to Will Shipley was fumbled, but that seemed to be a timing issue between Hurts and RB3 Next up? Two intense, long practices against the Patriots Day 12 Stats: 13/198, 0 TD, 0 INT 2026 Stats Overall: 138/199, 10 TD, 6 INT
